messages:
Maria Chen: quick heads up — i'm preparing a small change to how we handle encryption for DB snapshots + object-storage backups. want a quick pass on RBAC and KMS implications before i open the PR.
Alex Russell: thanks — can you summarize the user stories? is this about rotating CMKs, restricting decryptors, or changing key policy for the restore service?
Maria Chen: all of the above, tl;dr: 1) rotate CMKs quarterly for prod snapshots; 2) lock down decrypt to a new restore role instead of devs; 3) add explicit audit log markers for snapshot decrypt/restore operations.
Samir Patel: +1 on separating restore access. question: will the restore role live in the infra account or customer account? that affects key policy syntax and cross-account principals.
Maria Chen: restore role will be in the infra account (same account as restore runner). we'll add conditions to the key policy to only allow Decrypt/GenerateDataKey when request includes a valid SAML session tag and request originates from our restore service principal.
Alex Russell: do we have an example policy snippet we can use? also need to confirm CloudTrail captures KMS events for GenerateDataKey and Decrypt.
Maria Chen: here's the rough key policy i'll put in the PR comments:
```json
{
  "Sid": "AllowInfraRestore",
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/restore-service"},
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"],
  "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"aws:RequestTag/restore-run": "true"}}
}
```
Samir Patel: looks good. add an explicit Deny for any principal not in the allow list to make audit easier. also recommend `kms:ViaService` constraint for S3 restores.
Infra Bot: note — CloudTrail is enabled for kms.amazonaws.com in prod; log retention 90 days.
Alex Russell: for RBAC changes: we'll need an admin-level migration to update IAM roles, plus a short runbook for SREs to authorize emergency restores. this should go through a short change window.
Maria Chen: planned change window: UTC 2026-04-02 02:00-03:00. will open a ticket with changelog and automatic rollback if errors seen.
Oncall: please add automatic alert if any decrypt calls fail with AccessDenied after rollout — that will indicate policy mismatch.
Samir Patel: vuln triage note — rotating CMKs can surface issues if any services cache plaintext DEKs; add a pre-rotate canary that attempts a decrypt/restore from a snapshot in a test account.
Maria Chen: good call. will add a canary job that: 1) creates small snapshot, 2) attempts restore with new key, 3) verifies checksums.
Alex Russell: audit logging — we want a high-level marker in our SIEM when a snapshot is restored. propose we emit an internal event on success (restore.complete) with fields: snapshot_id, requested_by, key_id, restore_job_id — and map that to an alerting rule for unusual volumes.
Maria Chen: agreed. i'll add a telemetry task. also adding the restore.complete event to the incident playbook so SOC can see it.
Samir Patel: one more: accessible backups in object storage — ensure SSE-KMS is enabled for all backup buckets and that bucket policies block PutObject without x-amz-server-side-encryption set.
Alex Russell: small snippet for S3 bucket policy to reject unsigned uploads is helpful.
Maria Chen: will drop examples in the PR. last check: any objections to enforcing RBAC change with a canary release first?
Oncall: no objections. i prefer staged rollout: one region, monitor 1hr, then global.
Maria Chen: thanks everyone — i'll open the PR with key policy, IAM change plan, canary job, and audit integration links. tagging for review: @Alex Russell @Samir Patel.
Alex Russell: will review today.
Samir Patel: lgtm pending minor policy Deny tweak.
Infra Bot: reminder — file created: docs/runbooks/restore-key-rotation.md (link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/restore-key-rotation)
